entry.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
entry.summary: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

entry.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
entry.summary: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$. In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

entry.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
entry.summary: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

entry.title: Irrationality of the conjugacy growth on Heisenberg groups
entry.summary: We demonstrate that the conjugacy growth series for the Heisenberg groups $H_n(\mathbb{Z})$ is never algebraic, irrespective of the generating set. This makes progress towards the conjecture that all finitely presented groups that are not virtually abelian have irrational conjugacy growth series. Contrary to the group $H_3(\mathbb{Z})$, where the conjugacy growth is $n^2\log(n)$, the conjugacy growth of the other Heisenberg groups is polynomial, making these groups the first known nilpotent groups where the irrationality does not follow from the asymptotic growth.

entry.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
entry.summary: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.

entry.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
entry.summary: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $γ_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/γ_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We disprove this conjecture for every $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.

entry.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
entry.summary: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.

entry.title: The_Quadratic_Conjecture_and_p-groups_of_maximal_class
entry.summary: The Quadratic Conjecture for finite p-groups, which is equivalent to the Strong Oliver Conjecture, asserts that if a finite p-group G acts faithfully on an F-module V, then the center Z(G) contains a quadratic element. In this paper, we investigate the structure of maximal class p-groups and establish that they satisfy the Quadratic Conjecture.

entry.title: Abelian quotients and orbit sizes for subgroups of linear groups
entry.summary: Keller and Yang formulated two conjectures relating abelian quotients of subgroups of finite linear groups to largest orbit sizes. After counterexamples were found to the original conjectures, two revised versions were proposed. We prove both revised conjectures for every finite group $G$ satisfying $F(G)=F^*(G)$. We also extend a regular-orbit theorem for nilpotent subgroups to completely reducible modules of mixed characteristic under the same hypothesis.

entry.title: Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups
entry.summary: We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.

entry.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
entry.summary: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.

entry.title: On the generation of the symmetric group by index relations of three prefix reversals
entry.summary: The cubic pancake graphs are Cayley graphs over the symmetric group Sn generated by three prefix reversals. There is the folllowing open problem: characterize all the sets of three prefix reversals that generate Sn. Blanco and Golubyatnikov give a complete solution of the problem when any of the two smallest or the two largest lengths but n are included in a triple of prefix reversals. According to their conjectures, we give some conditions implying a triple of prefix reversals does not generate Sn. Moreover, Using the symmetric groups that can already be generated by three prefix reversals, we can derive some recurrence conditions.
